AI.result: The outburst exhibited a steep 2.85 mag brightening in r-band over 4.6 months, preceded by a shallower 4-year infrared rise. Spectroscopy confirms an FU Ori-type outburst with a mixed-temperature accretion disk spectrum and blueshifted absorption lines indicating a strong wind.
AI.conclusion: The event is confirmed as a new FU Orionis-type outburst from a previously unstudied flat-spectrum YSO. The outburst source shows signatures of an accretion disk with wind-driven outflows.

title: DEM analysis of the 6 September 2011 large-scale coronal wave
summary: Large-scale coronal waves are globally propagating intensity enhancements in extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) and soft X-ray (SXR) observations, associated with solar flares and coronal mass ejections (CMEs). They are interpreted as low-coronal signatures of a large-amplitude fast magnetosonic wave. On 6 September 2011, a fast (v = 1000 km/s) large-scale coronal wave accompanied an eruptive X2.1 class flare. A segment of the wave front temporarily dissappeared in EUV channels sensitive to quiet-Sun plasma, while it remained visible in higher temperature channels. We apply differential emission measure (DEM) diagnostics to SDO/AIA EUV observations to derive local density, temperature, emission measure, and DEM distributions, and examine their temporal evolution during the wave passage. The wave passage causes increases of 6-8% in density and 10-18% in temperature. While the density increase is comparable to earlier reports, the temperature increase exceeds expectations. This indicates that the temperature enhancement cannot be explained by compressional adiabatic heating alone, and instead suggests the presence of additional heating mechanisms, such as magnetic reconnection or wave mode conversion. During the temporary disappearance of the wave, the plasma parameters at the wave front increase, but with a strong spatial variability, with density increases ranging from 1% to 10%. The initial temperature in the affected area is notably higher than typical quiet-Sun regions (T > 1.7 MK), which allows plasma to be heated beyond the peak response of the AIA 193 and 211 Åchannels. We conclude that the apparent temporary disappearance of the wave front is primarily due to the combined effects in the intensity of the CME-associated coronal dimming following the wave and the wave itself, with heating further reducing its detectability in channels sensitive to quiet-Sun temperatures.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes a fast (1000 km/s) coronal wave on 6 September 2011 using DEM diagnostics from SDO/AIA data. The wave causes 6-8% density and 10-18% temperature increases. The temperature rise exceeds expectations from adiabatic compression alone, suggesting additional heating mechanisms like magnetic reconnection or wave mode conversion. The temporary disappearance of the wave front in certain EUV channels is due to combined effects of coronal dimming and heating, which shifts the plasma response away from quiet-Sun temperature channels.
AI.motivation: To understand the physical nature of large-scale coronal waves by quantifying the thermodynamic response (density, temperature, emission measure) of the plasma during wave passage, particularly investigating why a segment of the wave front temporarily disappeared in certain EUV channels.
AI.method: Differential emission measure (DEM) diagnostics applied to SDO/AIA EUV observations to derive local density, temperature, emission measure, and DEM distributions, examining their temporal evolution during wave passage.
AI.result: The wave caused 6-8% density increases and 10-18% temperature increases. The temperature enhancement exceeds predictions from compressional adiabatic heating alone. During the temporary disappearance, plasma parameters increased but with strong spatial variability (1-10% density increases). The affected area had initial temperature >1.7 MK, higher than typical quiet-Sun regions.
AI.conclusion: The temporary disappearance of the wave front is primarily due to combined effects of CME-associated coronal dimming and wave heating, with heating reducing detectability in quiet-Sun temperature channels. Additional heating mechanisms beyond adiabatic compression are required to explain the observed temperature enhancement.

title: A Be-shell star rotating at the critical limit and a partially stripped companion in a post-mass-transfer solution for the eclipsing binary V505 Mon
comment: 6 pages including 2 tables and 4 figures. Accepted for publication in 2026, BAV Rundbrief, 3, 105
summary: In this study of the eclipsing shell star binary HD 48914 (V505 Mon) existing photometric and radial velocity data have been completed by an unbiased determination of the surface temperature of the companion star and new data from the TESS mission. For the mean effective temperatures in our equatorial view, polar/equatorial radii and masses we get about 16000 K (dimmed), 4.27 / 6.37 Rsun and 7.40 Msun for the Be star, and about 14400 K, 6.19 / 7.17 Rsun and 2.03 Msun for the companion star (a contracting hot subdwarf precursor). Their calculated rotational equatorial velocities both are surprisingly high: 467 km/s for the Be star rotating at its centrifugal limit as well as 131 km/s for its former donor star companion. The Be star is surrounded by a large equatorial decretion disk having a radius of about 65 Rsun and fits into the main sequence of stellar models at a sub-solar metallicity of Z = 0.006.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes the binary system HD 48914 (V505 Mon), finding a Be star (16,000 K, 7.40 M☉, rotating at centrifugal limit 467 km/s) and a companion hot subdwarf precursor (14,400 K, 2.03 M☉, rotating at 131 km/s), surrounded by a large decretion disk (~65 R☉) at sub-solar metallicity Z=0.006.
AI.motivation: To complete existing photometric and radial velocity data for the eclipsing shell star binary HD 48914 with an unbiased determination of the companion's surface temperature and new TESS mission data.
AI.method: Combined analysis of existing photometric and radial velocity data with unbiased temperature determination of the companion star and new TESS data; equatorial view modeling of effective temperatures, polar/equatorial radii, masses, and rotational velocities.
AI.result: Be star: ~16,000 K (dimmed), 4.27/6.37 R☉, 7.40 M☉, rotating at 467 km/s (centrifugal limit). Companion (contracting hot subdwarf precursor): ~14,400 K, 6.19/7.17 R☉, 2.03 M☉, rotating at 131 km/s. Decretion disk radius ~65 R☉. System at sub-solar metallicity Z=0.006.
AI.conclusion: The Be star is rotating at its centrifugal limit; the companion is a former donor star now a contracting hot subdwarf precursor; both exhibit surprisingly high rotational velocities.

title: Incorporating physical source parameters into microlensing modeling
summary: Modeling of complex microlensing events suffers from many difficult-to-disentangle degeneracies. This is especially the case for orbital motion of the source in a binary system, the so-called xallarap effect. To address the degeneracies inherent in xallarap modeling, we developed a novel approach that directly samples the physical parameters of the source stars (initial mass, evolutionary phase, metallicity, distance, and reddening) during MCMC fitting. In our approach the physical parameters of the source are estimated using MIST stellar evolution models. This parametrization imposes astrophysical constraints that help identify the physically most probable solutions. We test our method on the complex microlensing event OGLE-2017-BLG-0114, which exhibits signatures that can be traced to the complexity of the source system. We successfully constrained the microlensing models, achieving improvements in the Einstein ring radius estimates by up to an order of magnitude in the case of binary source models.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a novel MCMC-based xallarap modeling approach that directly samples physical source parameters (using MIST stellar evolution models) to break degeneracies in complex microlensing events, demonstrated on OGLE-2017-BLG-0114 with order-of-magnitude improvements in Einstein ring radius estimates.
AI.motivation: Complex microlensing events suffer from severe degeneracies, especially from the xallarap effect (orbital motion of the source in a binary system). Traditional modeling struggles to disentangle these degeneracies, motivating a physically-constrained approach.
AI.method: The authors developed an MCMC fitting approach that directly samples physical parameters of source stars (initial mass, evolutionary phase, metallicity, distance, reddening) using MIST stellar evolution models as priors, imposing astrophysical constraints to identify physically probable solutions.
AI.result: Applied to OGLE-2017-BLG-0114, the method successfully constrained microlensing models, achieving up to an order-of-magnitude improvement in Einstein ring radius estimates for binary source models.
AI.conclusion: Integrating stellar evolution physics directly into xallarap modeling effectively breaks degeneracies and yields significantly more precise physical parameter estimates in complex microlensing events.
